neighbours.label: the slot just before a personal-identifier noun ('name', 'identity', further details) when someone's identifying details are being asked for, recorded or withheld: fires on the possessive or comma before it ('did not release his', 'the driver's', 'phone number,'); possessives in everyday contexts stay quiet
fire: The woman was taken to hospital, and police have not yet made public her name.
He chatted with me for an hour and never once asked me what my name was.
On the first line of the form, print the applicant's full name in capitals.
The caller hung up before the operator could take down his name or address.
Each luggage tag should carry the passenger's surname and a contact number.
The newspaper agreed not to print the witness's name for her own safety.
To open an account we need your date of birth, home address, and mother's maiden name.
The teacher went round the room and asked every child to say their name aloud.
quiet: The woman was taken to hospital, and doctors have not yet set her broken arm.
He chatted with me for an hour and never once touched his cup of tea.
On the first line of the recipe, check the oven's temperature before you start.
The caller hung up before the operator could finish his sandwich or coffee.
Each luggage rack should carry the passenger's bags and a folded coat.
The newspaper agreed not to raise the paper's price for another year.
To paint a wall we need your ladder, some old sheets, and a wide brush.
The teacher went round the room and asked every child to close their book quietly.

notes: Card: ' and', ' your', ',', "'s", ' his' before '(first/last) name'; output promotes ' last', ' zip', ' full', ' hometown'. Probes: 'did not release his' 0.60, 'still don't know your' 0.43, 'phone number,' 0.41, 'driver's' 0.38, 'not disclosed his' 0.67; 'washed his car' 0.03, 'love your new haircut' 0.01. The pole fires before the noun, so the continuation does not matter; the near misses change the context that precedes the possessive.
